    The q-difference operator and the Gandhi polynomials #

    Elementary properties of the relation IsDelta f g (g = Δ_q f) in ℤ[q][x]: linearity, uniqueness of g, the values on monomials (Δ_q(x^{m+1}) = Σ_{i ≤ m} x^i (1 + qx)^{m-i}, equation (7.5)), and the existence of Δ_q f for every f. Consequently the q-Gandhi polynomials of both kinds exist and are unique (gandhiFirst, gandhiSecond).

    The last lemma, isDelta_X_mul_comp, is the substitution identity used in the proof of Theorem 8.5: for G = Δ_q g, Δ_q(x g(1 + qx)) = g(1 + qx) + q (1 + qx) G(1 + qx).

              The substitution identity of Theorem 8.5 #

              source
              theorem PretorsionImageClosed.Statement.isDelta_X_mul_comp {g G : Polynomial Rq} (hG : IsDelta g G) :
              IsDelta (Polynomial.X * g.comp U) (g.comp U + Polynomial.C q * U * G.comp U)

              For G = Δ_q g: Δ_q(x · g(U)) = g(U) + q U · G(U), where U = 1 + qx.
